verdict.summary: Round 2 finds no correctness, soundness, security, or test-validity defect. The manifest makes both planner features default-on and forwards them explicitly to sparq-engine; the README and matching agent-tools skill accurately document that public-surface behavior. The tests are meaningful for the integration contract: they pin the declared default set, compile against feature-gated engine APIs to witness forwarding, exercise the real MCP tools/call query path, verify IRI rewrite behavior and the literal-equality decline boundary, compare DP-enabled and scoped-disabled answers, and check planner scope restoration. The change adds no runtime dependency or uncaveated privacy claim. With no prior-round issues and no current issues, progress is stagnant under the required scale.
